name: Havana
description: The capital city of Cuba, known for its Spanish colonial architecture and classic American cars.

name: Kingston
description: The capital and largest city of Jamaica, located on the southeastern coast of the island.

name: Manila
description: The capital of the Philippines, a densely populated bayside city on the island of Luzon.

name: Reykjavik
description: The capital and largest city of Iceland, and the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state.

name: Tokyo
description: Japan's bustling capital on the island of Honshu, mixing the ultramodern and the traditional.

name: Dublin
description: The capital of Ireland, situated on the River Liffey at the mouth of Dublin Bay.

name: Wellington
description: The capital of New Zealand, located on the southern tip of the North Island.

name: Taipei
description: The capital of Taiwan, a modern metropolis on the Tamsui River on the island's northern tip.

name: Budapest
description: Hungary's capital, which is bisected by the Danube River and noted for its thermal baths.

name: Bangkok
description: The capital of Thailand, known for ornate shrines and vibrant street life along the Chao Phraya River.

name: Prague
description: The capital of the Czech Republic, divided by the Vltava River and nicknamed 'the City of a Hundred Spires'.

name: Warsaw
description: The capital of Poland, a major city on the Vistula River that was extensively rebuilt after WWII.

name: London
description: The capital of England, a 21st-century city with history stretching back to Roman times on the River Thames.

name: Paris
description: France's capital, a global center for art and culture set on the River Seine.

name: Cairo
description: Egypt’s sprawling capital, set on the Nile River and home to Ottoman mosques and the Egyptian Museum.

name: Vienna
description: Austria's capital, which lies on the Danube River and is known for its artistic and intellectual legacy.

name: Victoria Falls
description: A spectacular waterfall on the Zambezi River, named in honor of Queen Victoria.

name: Ho Chi Minh City
description: The largest city in Vietnam, formerly known as Saigon, it was renamed for a revolutionary leader.

name: Columbus
description: The state capital of Ohio, named for the Italian explorer Christopher Columbus.

name: Georgetown
description: The capital of Guyana, named in 1812 in honor of King George III.

name: Washington D.C.
description: The U.S. capital on the Potomac River, named for the country's first president.

name: Alexandria
description: A major port city in Egypt founded by and named for a Macedonian king and conqueror.

name: Lincoln
description: The state capital of Nebraska, named in honor of the 16th U.S. President.

name: Bismarck
description: The state capital of North Dakota, named in honor of a German chancellor to attract German investment.

name: Angkor Wat
description: A massive stone temple complex in Cambodia built by the Khmer King Suryavarman II.

name: Serengeti National Park
description: A vast ecosystem in Tanzania, famous for its massive annual migration of wildebeest and zebra.

name: Galapagos Islands
description: A volcanic archipelago in the Pacific Ocean, considered a living museum of evolution.

name: Yellowstone National Park
description: A nearly 3,500-sq.-mile wilderness recreation area atop a volcanic hot spot in the United States.

name: Machu Picchu
description: An Incan citadel set high in the Andes Mountains in Peru, renowned for its sophisticated dry-stone walls.

name: Pyramids of Giza
description: Iconic ancient structures near Cairo, Egypt, built as tombs for pharaohs.

name: Great Wall of China
description: A series of fortifications stretching across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states.

name: Venice
description: A city in northeastern Italy built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon in the Adriatic Sea.

name: La Paz
description: Bolivia's administrative capital, which rests on the Andes’ Altiplano plateau at more than 3,500m above sea level.

name: Quito
description: The capital of Ecuador, founded on the ruins of an Inca city at an elevation of 2,850m.

name: Bogotá
description: The sprawling, high-altitude capital of Colombia, located in the Andes mountains at 2,640m.

name: Thimphu
description: The capital of Bhutan, nestled in the higher ranges of the Himalayas at an elevation of 2,334m.

name: Mexico City
description: The densely populated, high-altitude capital of Mexico, built on the ruins of the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan.

name: Addis Ababa
description: Ethiopia’s sprawling capital in the highlands bordering the Great Rift Valley, with an elevation of 2,355m.

name: Cusco
description: A city in the Peruvian Andes which was once capital of the Inca Empire, sitting at an altitude of 3,399m.

name: Lhasa
description: The religious and administrative capital of Tibet, located at 3,656m and home to the Potala Palace.

name: Yangon
description: The largest city in Myanmar, which served as the country's capital until 2006.

name: Almaty
description: The largest metropolis in Kazakhstan, which served as its capital until 1997.

name: Lagos
description: The most populous city in Nigeria, which served as the nation's capital until 1991.

name: Zomba
description: A city in southern Malawi which was the capital of first British Central Africa and then Nyasaland until 1974.

name: Kyoto
description: Once the imperial capital of Japan, it's famous for its classical Buddhist temples, as well as gardens and palaces.

name: Rio de Janeiro
description: A huge seaside city in Brazil, which served as the nation's capital until 1960.

name: Istanbul
description: A major city in Turkey that was the capital of the Byzantine and Ottoman Empires.

name: St. Petersburg
description: A Russian port city on the Neva River, founded by and named for a Tsar, which was the imperial capital for 2 centuries.

name: The Grand Canyon
description: A massive natural gorge in Arizona, carved by the Colorado River over millions of years.

name: The Matterhorn
description: A famous mountain in the Alps, straddling the main watershed and border between Switzerland and Italy.

name: The Louvre
description: The world's largest art museum and a historic monument in Paris, France.

name: The Eiffel Tower
description: A wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France.

name: The Prado Museum
description: Spain's main national art museum, located in central Madrid.

name: The Colosseum
description: An oval amphitheater in the center of Rome, Italy, built of travertine, tuff, and brick-faced concrete.

name: The Kremlin
description: A fortified complex in the center of Moscow, which includes five palaces, four cathedrals, and serves as the official residence of the President of Russia.

name: The Acropolis
description: An ancient citadel located on a rocky outcrop above the city of Athens and containing the remains of several ancient buildings of great architectural and historic significance.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
description: A 19th-century Romanesque Revival palace in southwest Bavaria, Germany, commissioned by Ludwig II of Bavaria.

name: Winter Palace
description: The official residence of the Russian Emperors from 1732 to 1917, located in Saint Petersburg.

name: Catherine Palace
description: A Rococo palace located in the town of Tsarskoye Selo, commissioned by Catherine I of Russia.

name: Herodium
description: A truncated cone-shaped hill and fortress in the West Bank, built by Herod the Great between 23 and 15 BCE.

name: Taj Mahal
description: An ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna river in Agra, India, commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.

name: Versailles
description: The former principal royal residence of France from 1682, under Louis XIV, until the start of the French Revolution in 1789.

name: Forbidden City
description: A palace complex in central Beijing, China, that served as the home of emperors and their households for almost 500 years.

name: Alhambra
description: A palace and fortress complex of the Nasrid dynasty located in Granada, Andalusia, Spain.
